item.title: Eyes On ‘Aggressive’ PA Drivers Through April 26
item.description: Think someone’s looking over your shoulder as you drive? Through April 26, you may be right. PA and NJ law enforcers have begun aggressive driving enforcement.

item.title: How Long Have You Been Where You’ve Been?
item.description: How long have you lived in your TriCounty region home? Recent research suggests the statistics of home-owner longevity are changing. See how you measure up.

item.title: May Children’s Day on Boone Homestead Calendar
item.description: A day devoted to children's entertainment and historic adventure is planned for May 3 from noon to 4 p.m. at the Daniel Boone Homestead in Birdsboro.

item.title: Pottstown ‘Rock The Block’ Celebrates Earth Day
item.description: Join dozens of other volunteers and local non-profit groups to clean-up sites in Pottstown on April 25 (Saturday), to mark the 56th anniversary of Earth Day.

item.title: Foodie: ‘Best Chicken’ Label Awarded Again in Collegeville
item.description: Charlotte Street Coffee, in Pottstown and Boyertown, is part of a new partnership. Also, Speck’s in Collegeville is honored, again, for its chicken.

item.title: 2026 Pottstown Nights’ Shows Scheduled by Red Horse
item.description: Pottstown Nights Car Shows sponsored by the Red Horse Motoring Club will return monthly from May through September 2026 to the borough’s downtown.

item.title: Dunkin’ Regional Scholarships Program Returns
item.description: Twenty students in the greater Philadelphia area have opportunities to win $5,000 scholarships. Dunkin’ and its franchisees are making it possible.

item.title: Outlets Host Four-Day Spring Carnival, Midway
item.description: The Philadelphia Premium Outlets will host a spring carnival and midway April 9-12 (Thursday through Sunday) near its Nike and Five Below stores.

item.title: Two Area National Parks Offer Programs for Artists
item.description: If nature is your source of artistic inspiration, don’t miss the “Arts In The Parks” programs coming to Valley Forge and Hopewell Furnace.

item.title: Book Club Explores ‘God of the Woods’ in April
item.description: A literary thriller that won an award and national best-book honors is the April 18 book club choice in Lower Frederick Township. Come join its discussion.

item.title: Counties Plan Hazardous Household Waste Events
item.description: Montgomery, Chester, and Berks counties all have scheduled events at which residents can recycle hazardous household waste. Appointments are required.

item.title: Ciresi Proposes to Prohibit Data Center ‘NDAs’
item.description: Non-disclosure agreements between developers and governments keep needed information out of the public eye, Rep. Joe Ciresi says. He hopes to prohibit them.

item.title: Schwenkfelder Offers Free History Discussion Sunday
item.description: Learn Sunday about a strong connection between a 1900s Berks County community and Pennsburg, at a time when the distance between them was substantial.

item.title: MontCo Unclaimed Property Day (x2) Set for May 11
item.description: Think the state has some of your money, or maybe a jewel or two? Find out during Unclaimed Property Day (May 11) in Pottstown and Trappe.
